name: Customer Identification Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal policy governing customer identification and Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures. The policy is owned by the Head of Compliance and applies to all staff, branch managers, compliance, and risk personnel. It is mandated by FCA COBS Part 10 and the Money Laundering Regulations 2017, and was effective from 2026-01-15 with a scheduled review date of 2027-01-15.

Audience | All Staff, Branch Managers, Compliance, Risk

context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 10, Money Laundering Regulations 2017

name: Money Laundering Regulations 2017
description: UK legislation establishing anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing obligations, including customer identification and due diligence requirements. This regulation mandates the Customer Identification Policy.

name: Identity Verification Procedures
description: Policy governing the acceptable identity documents and verification methods for UK and non-UK customers during the KYC process. Specifies document types, validity requirements, and verification mechanisms including direct examination, certified copies, and DVLA online checks.
context: Verification method: Direct examination or certified copy
scope_summary: Establishes acceptable identity documents and verification methods for UK and non-UK customers during account opening and KYC processes
core_policy_statement: Identity verification must be performed using acceptable primary documents via direct examination, certified copy, or approved online verification methods

name: UK Passport
description: Valid, non-expired UK passport accepted as primary identity document for UK customers. Document verification includes examination of signature, photo, and personal details through direct examination or certified copy.
context: Document check: Signature, photo, personal details
Verification method: Direct examination or certified copy

name: UK Driving License
description: Valid, non-expired UK photocard driving license accepted as primary identity document for UK customers. Document verification includes photo, signature, address, and driving record checks via DVLA online verification.
context: UK Driving License — Valid, not expired, photocard
Document check: Photo, signature, address, driving record

name: UK National ID Card
description: Valid, non-expired UK National ID Card accepted as primary identity document for UK customers when introduced. Conditional acceptance pending formal introduction of this document type.
context: UK National ID Card — Valid, not expired (when introduced)

name: Foreign Passport
description: Foreign passport from English-speaking countries accepted as primary identity document for non-UK customers. Preference given to passports from English-speaking jurisdictions.

name: EU Driving License
description: EU-equivalent driving license accepted as primary identity document for non-UK customers. Equivalent to UK photocard driving license in terms of acceptable verification standards.

name: EU National ID Card
description: EU-equivalent national ID card accepted as primary identity document for non-UK customers. Equivalent to UK national ID card standards.

name: Direct Examination of Identity Documents
description: Verification method requiring direct physical examination of identity documents by bank staff. Applicable to UK passports and driving licenses as part of the primary KYC verification process.
context: Verification method: Direct examination or certified copy

name: UK Customer
description: Customer resident in or domiciled in the United Kingdom subject to UK-specific identity verification requirements. Must provide valid UK passport, UK driving license, or UK national ID card.
context: UK Driving License — Valid, not expired, photocard
context_role: domestic customer subject to UK identity verification requirements

name: Customer Identification Process
description: A four-step customer identification procedure encompassing document collection, physical verification, system recording, and channel-specific verification methods. The process requires examination of primary identification documents, assessment of document integrity, photo matching, and signature verification, with different assurance levels applied based on the account opening channel (branch, online, or postal).
context: Examine original document in person (branch opening) or certified copy (postal)
Verify photo matches customer appearance (if in-person)
Record document type, number, issue/expiry dates in AMS (Account Management System)

name: Primary Identification Document
description: The main identity document collected from the customer during account opening, subject to integrity assessment, expiry verification, and recording in the Account Management System. The document must be examined for tampering or alterations and linked to the customer record.
context: Collect document ID, issue date, expiry date

name: Certified Copy
description: A notarized or certified copy of the primary identification document submitted by customers opening accounts online or via postal channels. Certified copies are subject to automated validation and manual review by Compliance staff.
context: Examine original document in person (branch opening) or certified copy (postal)
Customer sends certified copy by registered mail

name: Document Integrity Assessment
description: A control measure requiring staff to assess identification documents for signs of tampering, alterations, or damage during the document collection phase. This assessment is performed as part of Step 1 of the identification process.
context: Examine original document in person (branch opening) or certified copy (postal)

name: Photo Matching Verification
description: A control measure requiring staff to verify that the photograph on the identification document matches the customer's appearance during in-person branch opening. This verification is performed as part of Step 2 of the identification process.
context: Verify photo matches customer appearance (if in-person)

name: Signature Verification
description: A control measure requiring staff to verify that the signature on the identification document matches the customer's specimen signature. This verification is performed as part of Step 2 of the identification process.

name: Document Expiry Verification
description: A control measure requiring staff to confirm that the identification document has not expired before accepting it for KYC purposes. This verification is performed as part of Step 2 of the identification process.
context: Collect document ID, issue date, expiry date

name: Account Management System Recording
description: A control measure requiring staff to record identification document details (type, number, issue and expiry dates) in the Account Management System and link the document to the customer's identification record. Any concerns identified during verification are flagged for manual review.
context: Record document type, number, issue/expiry dates in AMS (Account Management System)
Flag any concerns for manual review

name: Automated Document Validation
description: An optional automated control measure available for online account openings to validate certified copies of identification documents before manual review by Compliance staff.

name: Address Verification Cross-Reference
description: A control measure requiring staff to cross-reference the customer's address with the identification document during postal account opening verification. This is performed as part of the postal verification channel procedure.

name: Follow-Up Verification Call
description: A recommended control measure for postal account openings involving a follow-up verification call to the customer to confirm identity and address details. This provides additional assurance for lower-assurance postal opening channels.

name: Branch Staff
description: Staff members responsible for conducting in-person identification verification during branch account openings. Their responsibilities include examining original documents, verifying photo matches, checking signatures, and recording verification details with their name and date.

name: Compliance Staff
description: Staff members responsible for manual review of identification documents submitted through online and postal account opening channels. They conduct document validation, flag concerns for escalation, and record verification details with their name and date.

name: Branch Account Opening
description: An account opening conducted in person at a branch location, subject to the highest assurance identification verification procedures including physical examination of original documents and immediate in-person photo and signature verification.

name: Address Verification
description: The process of verifying a customer's address using acceptable documentary evidence. The policy establishes a tiered approach with primary preferred documents (utility bills, council tax documents, bank statements) and secondary alternatives when primary documents are unavailable. All primary documents must be current and match the customer's name and address.
context: Primary (Preferred): Utility Bill — Gas, electricity, water, telephone
Requirement: Current bill (dated within last 3 months)
Check: Matches customer name and address
consequence_of_failure: Customer cannot proceed with account opening

name: Utility Bill
description: An acceptable primary address verification document covering gas, electricity, water, or telephone bills. Must be current (dated within the last 3 months), match the customer's name and address, and be issued by a major supplier only.
context: Utility Bill — Gas, electricity, water, telephone
Requirement: Current bill (dated within last 3 months)
Check: Matches customer name and address
verification_method: Physical inspection to match customer name and address

name: Council Tax Document
description: An acceptable primary address verification document comprising a council tax bill or banding notice. Must be from the current year and match the customer's name and address.
context: Council Tax Document — Council tax bill or banding notice
verification_method: Physical inspection to match customer name and address

name: Bank Statement
description: An acceptable primary address verification document from another bank. Must be current (within 3 months) and show the customer's name and address. Cannot be accepted as sole evidence if the customer holds an account with the bank conducting the verification.
context: Limitation: Not accepted as sole evidence if customer has account with us
verification_method: Physical inspection to show customer name and address
exception_handling: Not accepted as sole evidence if customer has account with this bank

name: Mortgage Statement
description: An acceptable secondary address verification document used when primary documents are unavailable.

name: Tenancy Agreement
description: An acceptable secondary address verification document. Must be signed and include landlord details.

name: Insurance Policy
description: An acceptable secondary address verification document covering buildings or contents insurance policies.

name: HM Revenue & Customs Correspondence
description: An acceptable secondary address verification document comprising official correspondence from HM Revenue & Customs.

name: Electoral Register Extract
description: An acceptable secondary address verification document comprising an extract from the electoral register.

name: Primary Document Acceptance Requirement
description: Mandates that primary address verification documents (utility bills, council tax documents, or bank statements) must be current and match the customer's name and address exactly.
context: Check: Matches customer name and address
Requirement: Current bill (dated within last 3 months)
verification_method: Physical inspection to match customer name and address

name: Bank Statement Sole Evidence Prohibition
description: Prohibits the acceptance of a bank statement as sole evidence of address verification if the customer holds an account with the bank conducting the verification.
context: Limitation: Not accepted as sole evidence if customer has account with us
applies_to: Bank Statement as sole address verification document
consequence_of_breach: Bank statement cannot be accepted as only evidence of address for customers with existing account at this bank
exceptions: Bank statement may be used if customer does not have account with this bank

name: Utility Bill Currency Requirement
description: Requires that utility bills used for address verification must be dated within the last 3 months.
context: Requirement: Current bill (dated within last 3 months)

name: Council Tax Document Currency Requirement
description: Requires that council tax documents used for address verification must be from the current year.
context: Council Tax Document — Council tax bill or banding notice

name: Bank Statement Currency Requirement
description: Requires that bank statements used for address verification must be current (dated within 3 months).

name: Major Supplier Requirement for Utility Bills
canonical_name: Major Supplier Requirement for Utility Bills
key: major supplier requirement for utility bills|POLICY_PROVISION|banking.policy
description: Mandates that utility bills accepted for address verification must be issued by major suppliers only.
consequence_of_breach: Utility bill from non-major supplier will not be accepted for address verification

name: Signed Tenancy Agreement with Landlord Details
canonical_name: Signed Tenancy Agreement with Landlord Details
key: signed tenancy agreement with landlord details|POLICY_PROVISION|banking.policy
description: Requires that tenancy agreements used as secondary address verification documents must be signed and include landlord details.
consequence_of_breach: Unsigned tenancy agreement or agreement without landlord details will not be accepted

name: Address Verification Process
description: A three-step Know Your Customer process for verifying customer address information. The process involves collecting address verification documents, comparing addresses across ID and supporting documents, confirming UK or approved jurisdiction residency, and recording results in the system with flagging of discrepancies.
context: Compare address on ID document with address on supporting document
Confirm address is within UK (or approved jurisdiction)
Record address document type and date in system

name: Address Verification Document
description: A supporting document used to verify a customer's address during the KYC process. The document type and date are recorded and compared against the address shown on the customer's ID document.
context: Record document type, date, address shown
Compare address on ID document with address on supporting document

name: ID Document
description: An official identity document containing the customer's address, used as the primary reference point in address verification. The address shown on the ID document is compared against supporting address verification documents.
context: Compare address on ID document with address on supporting document
Record document type, date, address shown

name: Address Discrepancy Flagging
description: A control mechanism that flags any discrepancies identified during the address verification process. Discrepancies between ID document address and supporting document address are recorded in the system for review and investigation.

name: UK Postcode Format Validation
description: A validation control that confirms the address postcode conforms to the UK postcode format specification A(1,2)9(1,2)A 9A(2). This ensures address data quality and confirms UK residency or approved jurisdiction status.
context: Confirm address is within UK (or approved jurisdiction)

name: Address System Recording
description: A system-based control that records address verification document type and date, and links the verified address to the business ontology Address entity. This ensures audit trail and data integrity for address verification outcomes.
context: Record address document type and date in system

name: Low Risk Customer
description: Customer profile characterised by age 18–65, UK nationality, UK address, standard product usage, absence of adverse media, non-PEP status, and no high-value transactions. Represents the baseline risk tier for customer assessment.
context: Low Risk: Age 18–65, UK national, UK address, Standard products (savings, current account), No adverse media, Not PEP, No high-value transactions
risk_definition: Customer meeting standard low-risk criteria: UK national aged 18–65 with UK address, using standard products, no adverse media, not PEP, no high-value transactions
examples: Standard savings or current account user
required_response: Standard KYC and AML screening

name: Medium Risk Customer
description: Customer profile characterised by age outside standard range (>65 or <18, with >16 allowed for limited products), non-UK residence with UK citizenship, higher-value accounts exceeding £100k, professional or business customer status, or minor PEP connections.
context: Medium Risk: Age >65 or <18 (>16 allowed for limited products), Non-UK resident but UK citizen, Higher-value account (>£100k), Professional or business customer, Minor PEP connections
risk_definition: Customer with elevated risk factors: age outside standard range, non-UK residency, higher account balances, professional/business status, or minor PEP connections
examples: Age >65 or <18 (>16 allowed for limited products)
required_response: Enhanced due diligence and ongoing monitoring

name: High Risk Customer
description: Customer profile characterised by non-UK citizenship with foreign address, significant PEP exposure, unclear beneficial ownership, transaction patterns suggesting elevated risk, residence in OFAC/sanctions-listed countries, identified adverse media, or compliance referral.
context: High Risk: Non-UK citizen with foreign address, Significant PEP exposure, Beneficial owner unclear, Transaction pattern suggests higher risk, Country of residence on OFAC/sanctions list, Adverse media identified, Referred by Compliance
risk_definition: Customer with significant risk indicators: non-UK citizenship with foreign address, substantial PEP exposure, unclear beneficial ownership, suspicious transaction patterns, OFAC/sanctions list residence, adverse media, or compliance referral
examples: Country of residence on OFAC or sanctions list
required_response: Enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, enhanced ongoing monitoring, potential SAR filing

name: Savings Account Product
description: Standard savings product referenced as a low-risk product category in the risk-based customer assessment framework.

name: PEP Screening
description: Politically Exposed Person screening obligation integrated into risk-based customer assessment. Customers with no PEP status are classified as low risk, minor PEP connections elevate to medium risk, and significant PEP exposure triggers high-risk classification.
detection_mechanism: PEP database check at onboarding and periodic review
risk_indicator: PEP status elevates customer risk classification

name: Individual Customer
description: Natural person subject to risk-based customer assessment framework. Risk classification determines the intensity of due diligence, monitoring, and ongoing compliance obligations.

name: Beneficial Owner
description: Ultimate beneficial owner of an account or customer relationship. Unclear beneficial ownership is a high-risk indicator requiring enhanced due diligence.
risk_indicator: Unclear beneficial ownership elevates customer to high risk

name: Risk-Based Customer Assessment
description: Structured Know Your Customer assessment process that categorises customers into low, medium, or high risk tiers based on demographic, geographic, product, transaction, and compliance factors. Assessment determines the scope and intensity of ongoing due diligence obligations.

name: High-Value Transaction
description: Transaction activity referenced as a risk indicator. Absence of high-value transactions is a low-risk indicator, while higher-value accounts exceeding £100k elevate risk classification.
risk_indicator: High-value transactions elevate customer risk classification

name: Transaction Pattern Assessment
description: Ongoing assessment of customer transaction patterns as part of risk-based customer evaluation. Transaction patterns suggesting higher risk trigger high-risk classification.
risk_indicator: Transaction pattern suggesting higher risk elevates customer to high risk

name: Risk-Based Re-verification Policy
description: A policy establishing a risk-based schedule for periodic re-verification of customer identity and address information. Re-verification frequency is tiered according to customer risk classification, ranging from every 5 years for low-risk customers to annual or on-transaction basis for high-risk customers.
core_policy_statement: Customer identity and address verification shall be conducted on a risk-based schedule, with frequency determined by the customer's risk classification
scope_summary: Applies to periodic re-verification of existing customers classified as low, medium, or high risk

name: Low-Risk Customer Re-verification Frequency
description: Mandatory requirement that customers classified as low-risk must undergo re-verification of identity and address information every 5 years.

name: Medium-Risk Customer Re-verification Frequency
description: Mandatory requirement that customers classified as medium-risk must undergo re-verification of identity and address information every 3 years.

name: High-Risk Customer Re-verification Frequency
description: Mandatory requirement that customers classified as high-risk must undergo re-verification of identity and address information annually or on a per-transaction basis.

name: Customer Risk Classification
description: A risk categorisation framework used to determine the frequency and intensity of customer re-verification obligations. The policy defines three risk tiers: low, medium, and high, each with corresponding re-verification schedules.
risk_definition: Categorization of customers into risk tiers (low, medium, high) that determines the frequency of identity and address re-verification

name: Periodic Identity and Address Re-verification
description: The ongoing process of re-verifying customer identity and address information at intervals determined by the customer's risk classification. This control ensures that customer information remains current and accurate throughout the customer lifecycle.
timing_or_refresh_frequency: risk-based: low-risk every 5 years, medium-risk every 3 years, high-risk annually or on-transaction basis

name: Low-Risk Customer
description: A customer classified as presenting low compliance risk, subject to re-verification of identity and address information every 5 years under the risk-based re-verification policy.

name: High-Risk Customer
description: A customer classified as presenting high compliance risk, subject to re-verification of identity and address information annually or on a per-transaction basis under the risk-based re-verification policy.
eligibility_or_verification_status: re-verification required annually or on-transaction basis

name: Enhanced Due Diligence Policy
description: Policy mandating Enhanced Due Diligence procedures for high-risk customers and specific trigger scenarios. Establishes mandatory verification procedures, escalation requirements, and ongoing monitoring obligations for customers presenting elevated compliance risk.
context: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Mandatory for high-risk customers and certain scenarios

EDD Procedures: 1. Enhanced identity verification (multiple documents) 2. Beneficial ownership verification (if customer is entity) 3. Source of funds verification 4. Ongoing transaction monitoring 5. Periodic review (annual minimum) 6. Documentation of risk assessment
Escalation: Compliance Head approval required for EDD customers
core_policy_statement: Enhanced Due Diligence is mandatory for high-risk customers and certain scenarios including customers from high-risk countries, PEPs, unclear beneficial ownership, unusual transaction patterns, complaint or fraud history, and identified regulatory concerns.
scope_summary: Applies to high-risk customers and specific trigger scenarios; includes identity verification, beneficial ownership verification, source of funds verification, ongoing transaction monitoring, periodic review, and risk assessment documentation.
